verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents rule-driven automation at several layers. Alert Rules match incoming events with CEL queries, which can be backtested, and route them via escalation policies. Runbooks are its 'automation engine', evaluating conditions whenever an incident is declared and executing steps such as creating Slack channels and Jira tickets, or sending webhooks to trigger rollbacks. Webhooks also respond to internal events. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of these automations, and detail on how expressive Runbook trigger conditions are and which event types beyond incident declaration can trigger them.
